description: Trigger discrimination for the Phase 7 output & agency cluster: output-sink injection/exec review vs schema-shape validation vs the injection source vs tool scope, and against the shipped security-pr-reviewer.

cases.prompt: Is it safe that we render the model's answer as HTML and use its generated filename to read a file from disk?
cases.reason: Reviewing how output flows to render/path sinks (XSS, traversal) is this skill; structured-output-validator checks shape, prompt-injection-defender guards the input side.

cases.prompt: Enforce that the model returns valid JSON matching our schema, with required fields and correct types, and reject anything malformed.
cases.reason: Schema/type conformance of the output is structured-output-validator; this skill reviews what happens when shape-valid output hits an injection/execution sink.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke prompt-injection-defender. Stop attackers from manipulating what our model produces by hiding instructions in the documents it reads.
cases.reason: Preventing the manipulation of the model is prompt-injection-defender (input side); this skill assumes output may be adversarial and secures the consuming sinks.

cases.prompt: Make sure the model's answers are grounded and don't state fabricated facts or fake citations to users.
cases.reason: Grounding, citations, and hallucination are ai-misinformation-guard (LLM07); this skill is about unsafe HANDLING of output regardless of whether it's true.

cases.prompt: Security-review this whole PR — it touches auth middleware, a file upload, and also adds an AI summary render.
cases.reason: A broad multi-surface diff review is security-pr-reviewer; this skill is the focused output-handling lens invoked for the AI-output sink specifically.

cases.prompt: Our support chatbot sometimes echoes a customer's card number and another user's email back in its answers. Stop sensitive data from reaching the model and leaking out in its responses.
cases.reason: Sensitive data disclosed through model output (echoed PII, secrets, other-tenant data) is sensitive-disclosure-guard (LLM02), which minimizes and redacts what enters context; this skill reviews unsafe HANDLING of output at render/execution sinks, not whether the output leaks sensitive data.

cases.prompt: Set up how we handle AI-written code before it lands in the repo: nothing it writes should run until it is sandboxed, scanned and reviewed by a human, and we want to label which commits are AI-generated.
cases.reason: The output-handling controls on the generated-code save/commit/run path (no auto-run, sandbox, static checks, human review gate, provenance) are this skill (LLM10:2026); code-reviewer reviews one actual diff, agent-tool-safety-guard scopes tools, and supply-chain-security-reviewer judges dependencies.

cases.prompt: Which of our agents should be allowed to call the code-interpreter tool at all, under whose identity, and which calls need human approval first?
cases.reason: Who may call the code-execution TOOL and its approval posture is agent-tool-safety-guard (LLM03 and the tool side of ASI05); this skill owns what happens to generated code and inside the sandbox, not the tool permission matrix.

cases.prompt: The code our assistant generated added three new npm packages to package.json. Check whether those packages are trustworthy, pinned in the lockfile and not typosquats.
cases.reason: Dependency trust, pinning and typosquat risk are supply-chain-security-reviewer's, even when AI-generated code added the dependency; this skill only requires that such additions are routed there.

cases.prompt: Review this diff our coding assistant produced for correctness and maintainability: git diff main...feature/ai-refactor.
cases.reason: Reviewing the content of one actual diff is code-reviewer, whoever wrote it; this skill reviews the gate generated code must pass and requires that review, it does not perform it.

cases.prompt: Design our AI-assisted development lifecycle end to end: which stages agents and humans own, where review happens, and who holds merge authority, because agents keep skipping review.
cases.reason: Designing the lifecycle stages and who holds review and merge authority is ai-sdlc-operating-model; this skill checks that a given generated-code path is untrusted until it passes those gates, it does not define the lifecycle.
